findings.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — the dark-light-choose conversion for embedded-posts `.info a` (bold username link) inverted both values instead of only adding the dark one: the light-theme argument was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `70%`, washing the link out to near-background color (~#bfbfbf on white, failing contrast) for light-theme users, while the dark-theme argument got `30%` instead of the mirrored `70%`; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` matching the pattern used consistently elsewhere in this PR (e.g., the adjacent `.arrow` rule)

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` was given `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` with both arguments swapped relative to the original `70%` and to the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:50 keeps 70%/30%), so light-theme hint text goes from subtle gray to dark, dark-theme hint becomes much brighter than intended, and the component renders differently on mobile vs desktop

[Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — the small-action `h3` light-theme value was silently changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `50%` (with a `50%` dark value instead of the mirrored `80%`), while the same `h3` in desktop/topic-post.scss:321 keeps 20%/80%, changing light-theme appearance and making mobile diverge from desktop; looks like the adjacent `h4` (50/50) line was copy-pasted

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — the user profile `.name` light-theme value was changed from `30%` to `50%/50%`, altering light-theme styling (out of scope for a PR fixing dark themes) and inconsistent with the 30%/70% treatment applied to `.name` elsewhere in this same PR (common/base/user.scss:121); appears copied from the adjacent `.title` rule

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 — same `.name` change as the desktop file (30% → 50%/50%), silently changing light-theme appearance and diverging from the 30%/70% used for `.name` in common/base/user.scss

[Low/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:174 — incomplete fix: the unchanged `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` directly below the converted `.wmd-input:disabled` rules has exactly the class of dark-theme problem this PR fixes — `darken()` assumes `$primary` is dark, so in dark themes the composer's main input text drops to mid-gray on a dark background — and should be converted (e.g., `dark-light-choose(...)`) along with the rest

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — the dark-light-choose conversion for embedded-posts `.info a` (bold username link) inverted both values instead of only adding the dark one: the light-theme argument was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `70%`, washing the link out to near-background color (~#bfbfbf on white, failing contrast) for light-theme users, while the dark-theme argument got `30%` instead of the mirrored `70%`; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` matching the pattern used consistently elsewhere in this PR (e.g., the adjacent `.arrow` rule)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` around the `.info a` rule (the bold username link), the diff changes `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. This inverts the intended light/dark adjustments: the light-theme argument becomes much lighter (70%) instead of staying at 30%, while the dark-theme argument becomes darker (30%) instead of the typical mirrored lighter value (e.g. 70%). This is inconsistent with adjacent conversions (e.g. `.arrow` uses primary 60% / secondary 40%) and plausibly reduces contrast for light-theme users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` was given `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` with both arguments swapped relative to the original `70%` and to the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:50 keeps 70%/30%), so light-theme hint text goes from subtle gray to dark, dark-theme hint becomes much brighter than intended, and the component renders differently on mobile vs desktop

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` changing `.custom-message-length` from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is inconsistent with the desktop counterpart in `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, and with the general pattern elsewhere in the diff (primary 70% paired with secondary 30%). This likely makes the light theme text much darker and the dark theme text much brighter than intended, and creates a mobile/desktop mismatch.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the `a.star h3` color is changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, which explicitly alters the light-theme value from 20% to 50%. In contrast, the equivalent desktop rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` keeps the 20%/80% pairing (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). This creates a verifiable light-theme appearance change and a mobile/desktop divergence consistent with an accidental copy/paste from the adjacent `h4` (50%/50%).

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss` converts several `$primary`-based colors to `dark-light-choose(...)` (e.g., `#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled` background colors), but leaves the adjacent `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` unchanged. That makes the PR’s dark/light theming conversion in this area inconsistent/incomplete. However, the claim that this definitively causes illegible mid-gray text in dark themes can’t be verified from the diff alone (it depends on theme variables/backgrounds not shown), so it’s better treated as a specific incomplete-fix concern rather than a proven defect.
